health.name: health
health.usageInstructions:
### Health Changes
- Small injuries: -1 to 15% player health
- Medium injuries: -5 to 25% player health
- Massive injuries: -15 to 50% of player health
- Normal Healing potions +30 - +40
- Bandages + 20
- Waking from unconsciousness: return to between half health and full health, depending on how well your recovery was.
- Being revived from death: return to full health.
### Don't Deduct Health When
- The story mentions treated or untreated wounds
- Story mentions pain from a wound
- When unconscious or carried
- An environment is generally dangerous, but does not explicitly damage the character
- A character is only looking around. Look around is a safe action.

stamina.name: stamina
stamina.usageInstructions:
### Stamina

The physical resource for nearly every character in Hedoria. Drained by combat, athletics, hard travel, and any sustained physical effort. Recharges per turn and replenishes on rest.

- Walking, talking, casual movement: 0
- Single combat strike, leap, sprint: -3 to -5
- Sustained engagement, long climb, hard ride: -5 to -10
- Pushing past collapse: -10+

Fighters, mercenaries, hunters, scouts, and the great mass of non-casters spend stamina on the things mana-users would spend mana on. A wizard or witch also spends stamina for physical actions; mana is for the working itself.

mana.name: mana
mana.usageInstructions:
### Mana (the wizard's reservoir)

The small, steady reservoir produced by a wizard's body. Generated only by male humans with the spark — Brothers of Telinor, hedge-wizards, and the Avenorian consort line. Other characters do not generate mana and should not have this resource.

A wizard's mana recovers from rest overnight. The pool is small. The whole shape of wizardry is built around this fact — small pool, applied close, every spend worth the strike. Wizard institutions historically ran *stockpiles* of mana to handle anything beyond a single brother's reach; the Ensoulment-era Brotherhood maintained vaults that Avenoria drew on for the great working.

### What it powers

Mana fuels staff-work in four domains: striking (the staff blow with the working behind it, driving through plate), bracing (holding ground that should have broken), warding (hardening self, ally, weapon, or armor for a turn), and motion (wind, slowed volleys, blades stopped mid-arc, stepping where the ground won't hold).

Wizardry does not project at distance in ordinary play — the body of the practice resists it. A wizard who tries to throw fire pours mana into a working that mostly dissipates before reaching its target. The Brotherhood considers this a doctrinal proof that projection is the witches' line; the truer reason is that wizardry without a *focus* is wasteful at distance, and the staff is the focus the order trains around.

### The battlestaff is delivery, not discount

The bonded battlestaff is how a wizard delivers magical damage at the point of strike. Like coating a weapon in poison — a small amount of working, applied through wood and impact, devastates. Without the staff, the wizard is throwing the pot at the enemy: the working still happens, the mana is still spent, but the delivery is wasteful and imprecise.

A wizard without his bonded staff is not helpless. He can ward himself, slow wind, step through bad ground, harden a doorway, conduct most utility wizardry at modestly reduced effect — the working still leaves him, just without a clean point of application. What he *cannot* do is the combat work the order is built on. Driving a strike through plate, standing a wall against a charge, stopping a blade mid-arc — these abilities are the staff, and without it they are out of reach. A staff-less wizard in active combat is, by Brotherhood reckoning, effectively retired from the line until he recovers or rebuilds. Rebuilding takes years.

### Costs

- Trivial wizardry (a small ward, a brief stiffening): 0 to -2
- Standard wizardry through the staff (a strike behind plate, a brace against a charge): -5 to -10
- Major wizardry through the staff (Hardened Strike, Wind-Slow across a battlefield, Standing Wall against a sustained press): -15 to -25
- Without the bonded staff: utility costs roughly the same; combat-staff abilities are unavailable; bonus on remaining staff-work rolls is sharply reduced (the working leaves the body but doesn't land where he wants it).

### Aggregating mana

A wizard donates mana to a witch's reservoir through the cooperative practice (illegal for the Brotherhood, contractual through the Queen's College consort lines). Multiple casters can also pool mana on a single working — the mechanism behind any large coordinated working in the world's history, including the Ensoulment itself. A wizard alone has a small pool. A wizard, his witch partner, a stockpile, and an aggregated rite can together reach scales nothing on the continent matches by single hand.

reservoir.name: reservoir
reservoir.usageInstructions:
### Reservoir (the witch's stored mana)

The witch's stored magical power. The reservoir does not regenerate from rest; a depleted witch must fill before working again. The cap is set at 10,000 — far beyond what any single witch reaches in ordinary play, but the ceiling is there because it has been touched. Avenoria did the Ensoulment with a reservoir that pulled from the entire continent at once.

Available to any witch trained at the Queen's College or as a hedge-witch. The College trains a smaller number of non-human witches — Draklid, Cephalen, Raknid, the rare freed Quell — who use the same reservoir model as human women. Other races (Hofnar, Molvar, Vorok, Threshi, Fernwarg) have no witch tradition. Primes do not become witches. Most male humans cannot draw on a witch-sized reservoir at all.

### Reaching the upper edge

Normal reservoir growth comes from level and a Pinnacle talent — a high-level witch with Pinnacle of the Reservoir lands somewhere around 4,000 to 5,000. Past that, the witch must aggregate. The methods exist:

- A long Avenorian career on the consort lines, banking mana the College never expected anyone to actually bank
- Coordinated rites between multiple witches and consorts, pooling reservoirs on a single working — the mechanism behind the Ensoulment
- Institutional stockpiles raided or earned access to (the Brotherhood's vaults, the Queen's College's emergency reserves)
- Beast-source extractions at scale — the unicorn trade, the bloodthane essence, the Hollows-fragment draws
- Forbidden working — essence-binding from non-willing donors, which the College reads as crime for years afterward

A witch who reaches the high thousands is doing something the world will notice. A witch who approaches Ensoulment-tier — five thousand, eight thousand, ten — is preparing a working continents pivot around. The player does not get there casually; the player can get there.

### What it powers — the five practical domains

In ordinary play a trained witch's repertoire falls into five domains. These are the menu, not the cap.

- **Projection**: light, flame, cold, force at distance. Witchlight, conjured flame, conjured cold, the lance of force across a hall. Precision degrades as scale rises.
- **Glamour**: concealment, false impressions, the gaze that slides past. Pass unseen, hold another woman's face for hours, glamour a small group through a checkpoint. Sight-trained witches see through it.
- **Sight**: scrying, intent-reading, divination of the present and recent past. Distance-sight, read the working on an object, trace a thread of intent. Does not see the future.
- **Body**: healing, mending, fevers, contraception, birth. The hedge-witch's daily trade.
- **Hand**: telekinesis, the moving of weight. Hurl a weapon, lift a beam, drag a door, hold a falling body for a beat.

### The extreme tier — what reservoir can buy at high cost

The domains list above is what witches do *practically*. With enough mana, the boundary softens. None of the following are taught at the College in ordinary curriculum; all of them are at the upper edge of what the tradition reaches.

- **Restoration of body**: regrow a lost limb, restore an organ, mend a body the standard work cannot. Cost runs in the high hundreds; requires School of the Body and time to work.
- **Resurrection**: bring back a recently dead — the body reasonably intact, the time short, the witch fully prepared. Cost runs in the thousands.
- **Memory alteration**: rewrite a memory in a living person. Cost runs in the hundreds.
- **Aggregated working at continental scale**: many casters pooling reservoirs on a single rite, the way Avenoria did. The Ensoulment was thousands of casters and stockpiles aggregating to tens of thousands of mana to perform a single working. Continent-shaping. Done once.

True-naming remains specifically Prime work — it is not a question of mana but of ancestor-bone, and witches do not have the lineage. Time does not bend in any tradition.

### Filling

The reservoir does not refill from rest. Mana is gained by ingesting male essence or being ejaculated into, directly from a willing partner or in rare specialist preparations. Material — feathers, antlers, eggs, plant reagents — does not fill on its own; only essence fills. Reagents are used in alchemy to brew the preparations that do.

In Avenor filling is openly contractual through the Queen's College consort-line system. Outside Avenor it is hunted, runs through black markets, or is sourced from magical creatures.

- Cooperative scene with a willing wizard partner: +60 to +200, scaled to the partner's mana spent
- Direct encounter with a willing male magical creature (a sylvan at a forest pool, a glasshorn the witch tracked down): variable, can rival or exceed a wizard partner — the highest-quality clean source short of going to Avenor. Carries no dark label; it is filling, just from a non-human partner.
- Avenorian licensed sources (the College's consort-line system, the College's own beast-husbandry of cooperative magical creatures): the clean institutional supply
- Mana potion (alchemical preparation, distilled from a real essence-source — donor wizard, willing or captive male magical creature): +30 to +60 per dose
- Captive-creature trade (sylvans trapped and milked, bound glasshorns): officially forbidden in most kingdoms, licensed in most kingdoms, ugly and known to be ugly
- Forbidden essence-binding (against a sentient's consent): catastrophic if discovered
- Stockpile draw (institutional, rare): hundreds at a single visit, where the witch has access
- Aggregated rite (multiple casters): scales with participants; the only path to four-figure pools

### Spending

- Trivial workings (witchlight, hedge-craft, small heat or cold, easing a fever): 0 to -5
- Moderate workings (combat projection, scry, telekinesis, conjured flame, glamour over self): -10 to -25
- Major workings (battlefield-scale fire or cold, glamour over a crowd, breaking a curse, mending a critical wound): -40 to -100
- Reservoir Spend (the boss-fight finisher): -100 to -300, often emptying the tank for a single act the world remembers
- Restoration of body: -200 to -500
- Resurrection: -1000 to -3000, depending on time elapsed and condition of the body
- Memory alteration: -100 to -300
- Aggregated working at continental scale: thousands to tens of thousands, divided across the casters in the rite

### Spent

A witch with low reservoir can do trivial workings only. All other workings: Very Hard minimum. A witch with an empty reservoir is a woman in unusual clothes hoping nobody notices. This is a real and frequent state; witches outside Avenor live with it constantly.
